q: In public finance, 'fiscal space' of a Government refers to:

options.A: The physical space occupied by the offices of the Finance Ministry
options.B: The difference between the revenue receipts and the revenue expenditure of the Government
options.C: The room available in the Budget for providing resources for a desired purpose without undermining the sustainability of the Government's financial position
options.D: The gap between the fiscal deficit and the primary deficit of the Government

q: 'Fiscal consolidation' by a Government broadly means:

options.A: Merging the accounts of the Union and the States into a single account
options.B: A process of reducing the fiscal deficit and the public debt over the medium term, through measures on the revenue and expenditure sides
options.C: Presenting the Railway Budget along with the General Budget
options.D: Consolidating the Finance Accounts of the Union and the States into the Combined Finance and Revenue Accounts

q: The Guarantee Redemption Fund, set up by State Governments in accordance with the scheme advised for the purpose, is intended to:

options.A: Finance the capital works of the State Governments
options.B: Redeem the Ways and Means Advances taken by the State from the Reserve Bank of India
options.C: Provide grants-in-aid to local bodies of the State
options.D: Meet the obligations of the State Government in case the guarantees given by it in respect of borrowings of other bodies are invoked

q: The dated securities (Government securities) of the Government of India are ordinarily issued:

options.A: Directly by the Ministry of Finance to the subscribers at a fixed price
options.B: By the Comptroller and Auditor General of India through the Accountants General
options.C: Through auctions conducted by the Reserve Bank of India on behalf of the Government
options.D: By the State Governments through their treasuries

q: Which of the following is also a recognised means of financing the fiscal deficit of the Government of India, besides market borrowings and other debt receipts?

options.A: Appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.B: Collections under the small savings schemes credited to the Consolidated Fund
options.C: Recoveries of House Building Advances from Government servants
options.D: Drawdown of the cash balance of the Government

q: The Committee on Government Assurances of the Lok Sabha consists of:

options.A: 22 members — 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha
options.B: 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha
options.C: 10 members nominated by the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
options.D: 15 members nominated by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha

q: The Committee on Government Assurances of the Rajya Sabha consists of:

options.A: 10 members nominated by the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
options.B: 15 members nominated by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
options.C: 22 members drawn from both Houses of Parliament
options.D: 7 members elected by the Rajya Sabha

q: The Committee on Public Undertakings does NOT ordinarily examine:

options.A: The reports and accounts of the public undertakings specified for the purpose
options.B: Whether the public undertakings are being run on sound business principles and prudent commercial practices
options.C: Matters of major Government policy, as distinct from the commercial or day-to-day working of the undertakings
options.D: The reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India on the public undertakings

q: In the audit of stores and stock, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India examines, among other things, whether:

options.A: The shortages and excesses brought out in the stock verification sheets have been properly taken into account and regularised
options.B: Stores have in every case been purchased from the cheapest source available
options.C: The stock verifiers have been appointed by the audit office itself
options.D: The priced ledgers of the stores depots are maintained by the audit parties

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'supplementary audit' from 'test audit'?

options.A: Supplementary audit is the selective check of a part of the transactions, while test audit is the audit conducted over and above the audit of the statutory auditors
options.B: Supplementary audit is the audit conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India over and above the audit by the statutory auditors in the case of a Government company, while test audit is the check of a selected part of the transactions instead of a check of all the transactions
options.C: Both expressions mean the audit of only one selected month of the year
options.D: Supplementary audit is conducted by the internal audit organisation, while test audit is conducted by the Railway Board

q: The Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India on State Finances primarily presents:

options.A: The detailed accounts of each department of the State Government
options.B: An assessment and analysis of the overall financial position of the State Government, including its receipts, expenditure, debt and fiscal indicators
options.C: The audit objections relating to the State Public Service Commission
options.D: The appropriation accounts of the State public sector undertakings

q: In a State, the functions of compilation of the accounts of the State Government and of audit of those accounts are respectively performed by:

options.A: The Accountant General (Audit) and the Accountant General (Accounts and Entitlement)
options.B: The State Finance Department and the State Treasury
options.C: The Accountant General (Accounts and Entitlement) and the Accountant General (Audit), both functioning under the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The Examiner of Local Fund Accounts and the State Accountant General

q: Which of the following correctly brings out the nature of internal audit as distinguished from statutory audit?

options.A: Internal audit is an arrangement made by the administration itself for reviewing its own operations, while statutory audit is imposed by the Constitution and law and is conducted by an authority independent of the administration
options.B: Internal audit is conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, while statutory audit is conducted by the Accounts Department
options.C: Internal audit reports are laid before Parliament, while statutory audit reports are submitted to the head of the office
options.D: There is no difference between the two in nature or authority

q: The annual accounts of a Central autonomous body, whose audit has been entrusted to the Comptroller and Auditor General of India and who conducts a separate audit of them, are, along with his audit report on them:

options.A: Retained in the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: Submitted only to the Public Accounts Committee
options.C: Published in the Gazette of India by the body itself
options.D: Laid before Parliament

q: The annual accounts of a statutory corporation established by an Act of Parliament, not being a Government company, are audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India under the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 under:

options.A: Section 19
options.B: Section 13
options.C: Section 16
options.D: Section 24

q:
Consider the following statements about appropriation audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India:
1. It includes scrutiny of the re-appropriations made within a grant, to see that they have been made in accordance with the rules and by the competent authority.
2. It is confined to comparing the total expenditure of the Government with the total Budget provision of the year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India of the proforma accounts of a departmental commercial undertaking is directed mainly to satisfying himself that:

options.A: The undertaking has earned a profit in every year of its working
options.B: The proforma accounts have been correctly prepared and disclose the true commercial results of the working of the undertaking
options.C: The staff of the undertaking is adequate for its work
options.D: The undertaking has followed the pricing policy laid down by the Public Accounts Committee

q: In a performance audit conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, before the report is finalised:

options.A: The findings are voted upon by the Estimates Committee
options.B: The approval of the Finance Minister is obtained on every paragraph
options.C: The draft report is communicated to the Ministry or department concerned and its views and replies are taken into account in the final report
options.D: The report is published in draft form for public comments

q: In the case of a Government company, the comments of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India upon the accounts, made on conducting a supplementary audit, are:

options.A: Communicated only to the Ministry of Finance
options.B: Placed before the annual general meeting of the company at the same time and in the same manner as the report of the statutory auditors
options.C: Sent directly to the Public Accounts Committee, without being shown to the company
options.D: Published in the Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India on Union Government Accounts

q: Under the financial rules governing grants-in-aid, a further grant to a grantee institution is ordinarily not released unless:

options.A: The institution has earned a surplus in the preceding year
options.B: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India has certified the accounts of the institution
options.C: The institution has increased its own staff for the programme
options.D: The Utilisation Certificates in respect of the grants earlier released to the institution have been furnished

q: Under the original Separation Convention of 1924, the Railway Reserve Fund was maintained primarily so that:

options.A: The surplus of Railways in good years could be accumulated in it and drawn upon in lean years to meet the contribution payable to General Revenues and to tide over deficits
options.B: The Provident Fund balances of railway employees could be invested through it
options.C: The capital works of Railways could be financed exclusively out of it
options.D: The dividend payable to the shareholders of the railway companies could be paid out of it

q: Works financed from the Development Fund of Railways do not add to the capital-at-charge of Railways because:

options.A: The works financed from the Fund are of a revenue nature in every case
options.B: The Fund is fed by appropriations from the revenues and internal resources of Railways, and not by capital invested on which a return is payable
options.C: The works financed from the Fund are executed by the State Governments
options.D: The Fund is maintained in the Contingency Fund of India

q: The Capital Fund of Indian Railways is fed mainly by:

options.A: Market borrowings raised by the Indian Railway Finance Corporation
options.B: Grants-in-aid received from the State Governments
options.C: Appropriations made from the surplus and internal resources of Railways
options.D: The safety surcharge levied on passenger fares

q: The burden of the Social Service Obligations of Indian Railways is, in substance:

options.A: Reimbursed to Railways in full by the General Revenues every year
options.B: Met out of the Contingency Fund of India
options.C: Charged to the State Governments in which the loss-making services are operated
options.D: Borne by Railways themselves out of their earnings, principally through the surplus earned on freight traffic

q: In the classification of the accounts of the Union Government, the ordinary working expenses of Indian Railways, accounted for under Major Head 3002, fall under the sector:

options.A: General Services
options.B: Grants-in-aid and Contributions
options.C: Social Services
options.D: Economic Services

q:
Consider the following statements about the Railway Pension Fund:
1. Appropriations from the revenues of Railways are credited to the Pension Fund, whose balances are held in the Public Account of India.
2. The pensionary charges of retired railway employees are met by disbursements out of the Pension Fund.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh, like the other reserve funds of Indian Railways, is a fund whose balances are held in the accounts of the Government of India under:

options.A: The Public Account of India
options.B: The Contingency Fund of India
options.C: The Consolidated Fund of India – Capital section
options.D: A separate banking account of the Railway Board

q: The Zonal Councils, which are advisory bodies for matters of common interest between the Centre and the States grouped in each zone, are:

options.A: Constitutional bodies provided for in Article 263 of the Constitution
options.B: Statutory bodies set up under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956
options.C: Bodies set up by resolutions of the Cabinet from time to time
options.D: Committees of Parliament constituted for each zone

q: The Inter-State Council was set up as a permanent body, with the Prime Minister as its Chairperson, in pursuance of the recommendations of:

options.A: The Finance Commission
options.B: The Administrative Reforms Commission
options.C: The Sarkaria Commission on Centre-State relations
options.D: The Railway Convention Committee

q: In the accounts of the Government of India, the balances held by the Government with the Reserve Bank of India represent its:

options.A: Public debt
options.B: Revenue receipts of the year
options.C: Charged expenditure
options.D: Cash balance, with which the accounts of the year are opened and closed

q: In the accounts of a State Government, amounts set apart out of its revenues and credited to a fund in the Public Account for the amortisation of its open market borrowings are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 8000 – Contingency Fund
options.B: 8222 – Sinking Funds
options.C: 8443 – Civil Deposits
options.D: 6003 – Internal Debt of the State Government

q: In the accounts of a State Government, the loans and advances received by it from the Central Government are accounted for in the Consolidated Fund of the State under Major Head:

options.A: 6001 – Internal Debt of the Central Government
options.B: 7601 – Loans and Advances to State Governments
options.C: 6004 – Loans and Advances from Central Government
options.D: 8009 – State Provident Funds

q: In the accounts of the Union Government, loans and advances disbursed by it to the State Governments are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 7601 – Loans and Advances to State Governments
options.B: 6004 – Loans and Advances from Central Government
options.C: 7610 – Loans to Government Servants
options.D: 6217 – Loans for Urban Development

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Civil Deposits which bear interest are classified in the Public Account of India under Major Head 8336.
2. Civil Deposits which do not bear interest are classified in the Public Account of India under Major Head 8443.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Under Article 148 of the Constitution, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India can be removed from his office only:

options.A: By an order of the President on the recommendation of the Public Accounts Committee
options.B: By a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by a simple majority
options.C: On the advice of the Council of Ministers tendered to the President
options.D: In the like manner and on the like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court

q:
Consider the following statements about the Comptroller and Auditor General of India:
1. His salary and other conditions of service are determined by Parliament by law, and neither his salary nor his rights in respect of leave of absence, pension or the age of retirement shall be varied to his disadvantage after his appointment.
2. The administrative expenses of his office, including the salaries, allowances and pensions of the persons serving in that office, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A Central autonomous body earlier received its grants-in-aid in a lump sum and parked the unspent amounts in its own bank account. Under a revised arrangement, the funds remain with the Government and are released to the body through an assignment account with the Reserve Bank of India only at the time the payment actually falls due. This arrangement is an application of:

options.A: The Single Nodal Agency system for Centrally Sponsored Schemes
options.B: The Treasury Single Account system for autonomous bodies
options.C: The Ways and Means Advances system
options.D: The Consolidated Sinking Fund scheme

q: Borrowings raised by a public sector agency or special purpose vehicle, where the principal and interest are in substance serviced and repaid out of the Union Budget although the borrowings themselves do not appear in the Budget, have the effect of:

options.A: Understating the fiscal deficit and the liabilities of the Government disclosed in the budget documents
options.B: Increasing the revenue deficit but not the fiscal deficit of the Government
options.C: Improving the transparency of the public finances of the Government
options.D: Reducing the public debt of the Government in the Finance Accounts

q: In the organisation of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, the quality of audit conducted by the field audit offices is sought to be assured, among other measures, through:

options.A: Audit of the audit offices by the Ministry of Finance
options.B: Certification of every audit paragraph by the Public Accounts Committee
options.C: Peer review and quality assurance reviews of audit work against the prescribed auditing standards
options.D: Rotation of the Comptroller and Auditor General among the audit offices every year

q: Before a draft audit paragraph proposed for inclusion in the Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is finalised, the facts stated in it are ordinarily got confirmed by the Ministry or Department concerned through:

options.A: A vote on account taken from Parliament
options.B: A factual statement sent to the Ministry for verification of the facts
options.C: A reference to the Finance Commission
options.D: An inspection report of the resident audit party alone, without any reference to the Ministry

q: The Goods and Services Tax Compensation Fund, into which the compensation cess levied on certain goods is credited and from which compensation is paid to the States for loss of revenue arising from the implementation of the Goods and Services Tax, forms part of:

options.A: The Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: The Contingency Fund of India
options.C: A deposit account maintained by the Goods and Services Tax Council outside the Government accounts
options.D: The Public Account of India

q: The State Disaster Response Fund, constituted under the Disaster Management Act, 2005 for meeting the expenditure on immediate relief in response to notified disasters in a State, is maintained as part of:

options.A: The Public Account of the State
options.B: The Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: The Contingency Fund of the State
options.D: The Consolidated Fund of the State

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Government of India is required, under its agreement with the Reserve Bank of India, to maintain a minimum cash balance with the Bank.
2. Ways and Means Advances from the Reserve Bank of India are available to the Government to bridge temporary mismatches between its receipts and its payments when its cash balance falls short.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Government of India has no facility of overdraft from the Reserve Bank of India; it can only avail of Ways and Means Advances within the agreed limits.
2. Drawings by a State Government from the Reserve Bank of India in excess of its Ways and Means Advances limit constitute an overdraft.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: In the sanction of a Government scheme, a 'sunset date' signifies:

options.A: The date on which the Budget for the scheme is presented to Parliament
options.B: The date after which the scheme lapses unless it is appraised afresh and approved for continuance
options.C: The date on which the accounts of the scheme are finally closed by the Comptroller and Auditor General
options.D: The date from which the scheme is transferred to the State Governments

q: A district authority operates a Personal Deposit account in the Public Account of India for a specific purpose authorised by Government. A payment is to be made out of the balance at credit of this account. Which of the following correctly states the position?

options.A: The payment requires a fresh vote of Parliament in every case
options.B: The payment is a disbursement from the Public Account and does not require the vote of Parliament, the balance having already been credited to the account under proper authority
options.C: The payment can be made only after an Appropriation Act is passed for the amount
options.D: The payment must first be charged on the Consolidated Fund of India by a law of Parliament

q: Urgent and unforeseen relief expenditure has to be incurred immediately, but Parliament is not in session and no provision exists in the grants for the purpose. The expenditure is first met by an advance from the Contingency Fund of India. The advance so taken is thereafter:

options.A: Written off against the Public Account of India without any reference to Parliament
options.B: Adjusted against the balances of the Reserve Funds of the Government
options.C: Borne permanently by the Contingency Fund without recoupment
options.D: Recouped to the Fund after Parliament authorises the expenditure through a supplementary grant and the Appropriation Act

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Expenditure incurred by the executive in excess of the amount granted by Parliament for a service is regularised by Parliament voting an excess grant after the close of the financial year.
2. The excesses disclosed in the Appropriation Accounts are examined by the Public Accounts Committee before the excess grants are regularised.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: A Government office building is extended by constructing an additional floor, thereby adding to the accommodation and the value of the existing asset. In the Government accounts, the expenditure on the additional floor is treated as:

options.A: Revenue expenditure, because the building already exists
options.B: Capital expenditure, because it is an addition to, and improvement of, an existing asset
options.C: Charged expenditure on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: A deposit expenditure in the Public Account of India

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The separation of Railway finances from the general finances of the Government of India was recommended by the Acworth Committee.
2. The separation was given effect to from the year 1924-25.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: An audit engagement in which the auditor examines a programme simultaneously from the standpoints of economy in the acquisition of inputs, efficiency in converting inputs into outputs and effectiveness in achieving the intended results is, in substance, a:

options.A: Value for money (performance) audit
options.B: Financial (attest) audit only
options.C: Internal check of the accounts office
options.D: Stock verification by the Accounts Department

q: In the course of a financial audit, the auditor concludes that the financial statements give a true and fair view, but considers it necessary to draw the attention of the users to a matter which is already appropriately presented and disclosed in the statements and is fundamental to their understanding. The auditor should:

options.A: Qualify the audit opinion on the statements
options.B: Express a disclaimer of opinion on the statements
options.C: Resign from the audit engagement
options.D: Include an 'Emphasis of Matter' paragraph in the audit report, without modifying the opinion

q: The records of an audited office for the year under audit have been destroyed by fire, and the auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence by any alternative means, the possible effects of the limitation being pervasive to the accounts as a whole. The appropriate audit opinion in such a case is:

options.A: An unqualified opinion, because the loss of records was not the fault of the office
options.B: A disclaimer of opinion
options.C: An adverse opinion on the accounts
options.D: No report at all, the audit being abandoned permanently

q: In a divisional Accounts office, every salary bill is examined and passed for payment by an official other than the one who prepared it, so that the work of one official is automatically checked by another in the ordinary course. This arrangement is an instance of:

options.A: Internal audit
options.B: Statutory audit
options.C: Internal check
options.D: Performance audit

q: An amount recovered from a railway employee is held by the administration pending completion of an enquiry to determine the head of account to which it is finally creditable. Until the final head is determined, the amount is held under:

options.A: The Consolidated Fund of India as a final receipt
options.B: A suspense head of account
options.C: The Contingency Fund of India
options.D: The Capital Fund of Railways as an internal resource

q: Cash is transmitted by one disbursing officer of a Railway to another disbursing officer for making payments at the receiving end. In the railway accounts, such a transaction between the two officers is adjusted through:

options.A: A suspense head, because the final head is not known
options.B: The Pension Fund of Railways
options.C: A remittance head of account
options.D: The Block Account of the Railway

q: A researcher wishes to study, in a single publication, the consolidated accounting information of the Union Government and of all the State Governments taken together. The publication she should refer to is:

options.A: The Finance Accounts of the Union Government alone
options.B: The Combined Finance and Revenue Accounts prepared by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: The Appropriation Accounts of the Railways
options.D: The Budget at a Glance of the Union Government

q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India examines the systems and procedures relating to the assessment, collection and proper allocation of customs and other tax receipts of the Union, in exercise of his duty relating to:

options.A: Audit of stores and stock under Section 17 of the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971
options.B: Audit of grants-in-aid under Section 15 of that Act
options.C: Compilation of accounts under Section 10 of that Act
options.D: Audit of receipts of the Union under Section 16 of that Act

q: The annual accounts of a Government company of a State have been audited, and the Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India relating to them is ready. In accordance with Section 19A of the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971, the Report is to be:

options.A: Laid before the Legislature of the State
options.B: Confined to the Board of Directors of the company
options.C: Published only in the Gazette of India
options.D: Submitted to the Finance Commission for its comments

q: In a particular year, the whole of the fiscal deficit of the Government of India is accounted for by its interest payments, the primary deficit for the year being nil. This position indicates that:

options.A: The Government has borrowed only to meet its interest obligations, without any primary gap between its non-interest expenditure and its receipts
options.B: The Government has no public debt outstanding
options.C: The revenue deficit of the Government is necessarily nil
options.D: The Government is running a revenue surplus for the year

q: A guarantee given by the Government of India in respect of a loan raised by an agency is, so long as it is not invoked, a contingent liability of the Government. It becomes an actual liability of the Government:

options.A: On the date the guarantee is first given
options.B: At the end of every financial year, automatically
options.C: When the guarantee is invoked and the obligation devolves on the Government on default of the borrower
options.D: Only when the loan is fully repaid by the borrower

q: Over a few years of high inflation, and without any change in the rates or slabs of income tax, a large number of taxpayers find themselves paying tax at higher rates merely because their money incomes have risen with prices. This phenomenon is known as:

options.A: Crowding out
options.B: Fiscal drag
options.C: Tax buoyancy
options.D: Fiscal consolidation

q: In a recession, the tax collections of the Government fall automatically with falling incomes and its expenditure on unemployment-related support rises, without any fresh discretionary measure being taken, thereby cushioning the fall in demand. This happens because of:

options.A: Automatic stabilisers built into the fiscal system
options.B: Supplementary demands for grants voted by Parliament
options.C: Advances taken from the Contingency Fund of India
options.D: Re-appropriations made within the grants by the executive

q: A State Government maintains two separate funds in its Public Account: one built up for the amortisation of its open market borrowings, and another built up to meet the liability that may arise if the guarantees given by it are invoked. The two funds are, respectively:

options.A: The Consolidated Sinking Fund and the Guarantee Redemption Fund
options.B: The Guarantee Redemption Fund and the Consolidated Sinking Fund
options.C: The State Disaster Response Fund and the Contingency Fund
options.D: The General Reserve Fund and the Depreciation Reserve Fund

q: During a year, the gross traffic earnings of a zonal Railway increase, but its ordinary working expenses increase at a faster rate than the earnings. Other things remaining the same, the Operating Ratio of the Railway will:

options.A: Improve, that is, come down
options.B: Remain unchanged, because both earnings and expenses have increased
options.C: Cease to be computable for that year
options.D: Worsen, that is, go up

q: Two zonal Railways earn similar revenues, but one carries predominantly low-rated bulk traffic over long leads while the other carries a mixed traffic. A direct comparison of their Operating Ratios is considered misleading mainly because the Operating Ratio:

options.A: Is not expressed as a percentage of earnings
options.B: Does not take into account differences in the composition of traffic between different railways
options.C: Includes the appropriations to the Pension Fund twice over
options.D: Is worked out before the close of the annual accounts

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Link heads in the railway system of accounts serve to connect the Government accounts with the commercial accounts of Indian Railways.
2. 'Deposits with Reserve Bank', through which the cash transactions of Railways with the Government account at the Reserve Bank are adjusted, is one such link head.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements about the commercial accounts of Indian Railways:
1. In the Block Account, the assets of a Railway continue to be shown at their original capital cost.
2. Provision for the depreciation and replacement of assets is made through appropriation of revenues to the Depreciation Reserve Fund, and not by writing down the values shown in the Block Account.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Audit teams take up the audit of catering services simultaneously on several zonal Railways on a common theme, so that the results can be compared and the findings reported for the Railway system as a whole. Such an audit is best described as:

options.A: A theme-based audit
options.B: An internal check by the zonal Accounts Department
options.C: A supplementary audit of a Government company
options.D: A test audit of a single month of the year

q: During the discussion on the Demands for Grants, a member of the Lok Sabha wishes to draw attention to a specific grievance and proposes that the amount of a Demand be reduced by a token sum of Rs 100. The motion moved by the member is a:

options.A: Disapproval of policy cut motion
options.B: Economy cut motion
options.C: Token cut motion
options.D: Vote of credit

q: A document laid before the Public Accounts Committee shows, grant by grant, the final grant, the actual expenditure incurred against it and the explanations for the variations between the two. The document is the:

options.A: Finance Accounts
options.B: Demands for Grants
options.C: Finance Bill
options.D: Appropriation Accounts

q: In the middle of a financial year, a Ministry proposes to take up an altogether new activity involving substantial expenditure, which was not contemplated in the Budget for the year. Before the expenditure is incurred, the proposal is treated as:

options.A: A matter of mere re-appropriation within the existing grant
options.B: A 'new service', requiring the prior approval of Parliament before expenditure on it is incurred
options.C: Charged expenditure, which needs no approval of Parliament
options.D: An item to be met from the Public Account without any reference to Parliament

q: Savings are available in one part of a grant, and an administrative Ministry proposes to re-appropriate them to meet the cost of a new service which was not contemplated in the approved Budget. Such a re-appropriation is:
